newsitem.title: SPAIN: Focus - Spain's Endesa to buy two regional utilities.
newsitem.headline: Focus - Spain's Endesa to buy two regional utilities.

text.p: Spain's Endesa launched a friendly buy offer for two regional electrical groups on Friday in a government attempt at sprucing up the 66-percent state-owned group for complete privatisation by 1999.

Endesa will purchase up to 75 percent of Fuerzas Electricas de Catalunya (Fecsa) and of Sevillana de Electricidad at a price of 1,100 and 1,300 pesetas a share, respectively, for a cost of up to almost 200 billion pesetas.

The electrical generator -- which already holds 49 percent of Fecsa and 39.4 percent of Sevillana -- needs the two groups' regional distribution networks to help it cope with market liberalisation, analysts said.

"The 75 percent limit is a...maximum. What we intend to do is exceed 51 percent so the results are consolidated into the group," Industry Minister Josep Pique told journalists following the cabinet meeting at which the takeover offers were approved.

Endesa, the second most heavily weighted stock in Spain's IBEX index of 35 leading shares, needs to shape up quickly as planned deregulation of the market is expected to slash the profitability of Endesa's electricity generation business.
Pique said plans to liberalise the sector would be ready in a few weeks and added that the state will reduce its stake in Endesa to less than 50 percent before 1997.
The remainder would be privatised by 1999.
Control of the regional electricity companies would help expand Endesa's current 20 percent share of the distribution market, analysts said.

"Endesa is trying to diversify its operations and gain a hold in distribution. If it merges both subsidiaries it will achieve a reduction in costs," said Fabian Ramon at the Financial Savings Corporation.
Sevillana was considered a particularly attractive addition to Endesa because it is financially fit and controls the lucrative Maghreb gas pipeline.
Fecsa's financial state was less strong, but analysts said its hydraulic power assets and Catalan market were a plus.
Shares in Endesa rose 300 pesetas to 8,250 as the market greeted the deal warmly.
Shares in Sevillana and Fecsa also advanced. AT 1430 GMT, Sevillana was up 75 pesetas at 1,240, while Fecsa climbed 55 pesetas to 1,055.

But Standard & Poor's rating agency took a dim view of the plan. It said on Friday that it may cut Endesa's 11-plus local currency implied senior debt and AA foreign currency implied senior debt ratings because of the bid.
It said that although necessary, the investment was relatively large.
